selected_need: Make the discovered quality theory operational and AI-verifiable for human, AI-agent, and hybrid organizations.
intended_user_or_segment: Organizations with explicit quality documents, project histories, operations-only practice, or veteran-held tacit quality knowledge.
context_summary: Quality is defined as value realization within loss boundaries under uncertainty, not as output volume. The framework must support discovery, structure, evidence, verdicts, and governance across domains.
hypothesis: A schema-plus-workflow baseline with executable validation can convert QIF theory into repeatable quality evaluation behavior without requiring a production application.
rejected_alternatives: Application-first implementation before stabilizing the canonical model.
explicit_risks: The first baseline may overfit to abstract examples unless schemas and validator keep source, evidence, confidence, and verdict traceability explicit.
delivery_validation_requirements: Run a local validator against a sample QIF package and review the framework with Visionary, Builder, and Guardian perspectives.
need: Operationalize QIF quality theory into a verifiable framework.
intent: Produce canonical entities, schemas, workflows, governance, acceptance gates, and a validator.
context: Managed-project repository initialized with AOF v5.0.0; implementation must remain domain-general and must not treat activity counts as quality.
